$comment: Mutation arms cutting the types of package anyparse.check.common.control. Format and rules: docs/testing.md, Declared arms.

arms.name: M-INVERT-REGION-UNGUARDED
arms.note: a then-region closed only by the `else` is swapped into the tail slot with no terminator

arms.name: M-PTR-RIDES-NEVER
arms.note: a guard-line trailing comment no longer counts as riding its own branch, so the cascade narrowing refuses a fold the march would have carried correctly

arms.name: M-PTR-CASCADE-NEVER-STRANDS
arms.note: the cascade narrowing never fires, so an own-line comment between two rungs is hoisted off the gate it explains

arms.name: M-PIEC-SPINE-CLAIM-ANY
arms.note: every chain head reads as claimed by simplify-boolean-ternary, so the deferral fires on chains that check never touches

arms.name: M-TAILMERGE-NORM-ONLY
arms.note: statement identity is decided by whitespace-normalized source alone, so two calls differing only INSIDE a string literal read as the same statement and a tail that is not duplicated is reported

arms.name: M-TAILMERGE-FALL-KEPT
arms.find: for (c in node.children) visit(c, EMPTY_FALL, source, seams, out);
arms.replace: for (c in node.children) visit(c, fall, source, seams, out);
arms.note: the fall-through run is handed to EVERY node's children instead of being reset, so a loop body, a switch arm, a catch body and a lambda all look like they complete into the run after the construct

arms.name: M-NO-AUTOFIX-STILL-EDITS
arms.note: a rule declaring `NoAutofix` answers with an edit, so the declaration is a claim the run contradicts

arms.name: M-NO-AUTOFIX-REASON-IS-THE-RULE-NAME
arms.note: the declared reason is the rule name read back, which tells a reader nothing the id did not

arms.name: M-COLLAPSE-BINDER-UNPROVEN
arms.find: return CasePatterns.provesCaptureAt(arm, switchNode, node, resolve, scan.scope, scan.tree, seams.shape, typedSlot) ? node : null;
arms.note: a nested switch over a binder that may be a constant is spliced into the pattern

arms.name: M-CMPBOOL-RESOLVED-TYPE-PARAM-BLIND
arms.note: a member type or method return written `Bool` is proven a Bool even where a declaring type or method names a type parameter Bool

arms.name: M-DECLCHAIN-UNTYPED
arms.note: an unannotated declaration folds too, so its type comes from the if-expression's unified type rather than from its first write - measured to differ (`UInt` vs `Int`) and to stop compiling for a subclass in the first branch

arms.name: M-DECLCHAIN-INIT-ANY
arms.note: any initializer is relocated past the conditions, so a call, a read a condition could change, or an allocation runs after them instead of before

arms.name: M-DECLCHAIN-OCCURRENCE-COUNT
arms.find: if (Refs.find(name, head, s.shape).length != probe.leafCount) return null;
arms.note: any further occurrence of the target in the chain - a read in a condition or a value, a capture, a nested write - survives the fold, naming the variable inside its own initializer

arms.name: M-DECLCHAIN-LVALUE
arms.find: if (lvalue.kind != s.tree.identKind || lvalue.name != name) return null;
arms.note: a chain assigning another target folds into the declaration, which then takes that target's values

arms.name: M-DECLCHAIN-PREFIX-DANGLING
arms.note: a line comment ending the copied declaration prefix swallows the rebuilt ` = <value>;`

arms.name: M-DECLCHAIN-OWNED-BY-TERNARY
arms.note: every chain of plain assignments goes to the ternary rule, which builds its edit from the first branch alone, and the if-expression rule reports none

arms.name: M-DECLIF-CARRY
arms.find: final carried: Null<Carried> = IfExpressionChain.carriedComments(m.region, kept, m.probe.gaps, source, comments);
arms.note: the decl arm stops classifying the comments in its region, so one between the declaration and the chain is dropped by the rebuild

arms.name: M-DECLIF-PREFIX-KEPT
arms.note: the copied declaration prefix is no longer a kept span, so a comment inside it - which the prefix carries - refuses the site

arms.name: M-DECLTERN-NARROWING
arms.note: the decl arm collapses a null-narrowing guard onto bool literals, which the boolean simplification then flattens out of its narrowing

arms.name: M-DECLTERN-COMMENT
arms.note: the decl arm ignores comments outside its copied spans, so one in the `if` header is dropped by the rebuild

arms.name: M-PASSTHROUGH-TERNARY
arms.note: a ternary that only passes a nullable value through is written as `x != null ? x : null`, which prefer-null-coalescing then turns into the no-op `x ?? null`

arms.name: M-GUARD-ELSE-ADMITTED
arms.note: an `if` with an `else` is inverted as if it had none, so both guard rules drop the else branch

arms.name: M-GUARD-UNBRACED-THEN
arms.note: an un-braced then-branch is taken for a block, so its braces are cut off text that has none

arms.name: M-GUARD-MIN-THEN-IGNORED
arms.note: a then-branch under the rule's minimum is inverted, so guard-return flattens a one-statement branch

arms.name: M-GUARD-GLUE-COMMENT-BLIND
arms.note: a comment in the `if (` or `) {` glue no longer refuses the rewrite, which drops it

arms.name: M-GUARD-UNCLEAN-INVERSION-REPORTED
arms.note: a condition that can only invert into a `!( … )` wrap is reported, so the guard form reads worse than the nesting it removes

arms.name: M-GUARD-CONTINUE-DEFERS-STATEMENT-BLOCK-ONLY
arms.note: guard-continue defers to loop-guard on a statement-block body alone, so a do-while both rules read is reported by both

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-ANY-KIND
arms.note: any one-operand condition reads as a negation, so `a.b ? 1 : 2` is "inverted" to `b ? 2 : 1`

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-PAREN-KEPT
arms.note: the redundant paren around the negated operand is kept: `!(a || b) ? x : y` becomes `(a || b) ? y : x`

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-OVERLOAD-BLIND
arms.note: an `@:op(!A)` overload is ignored, so a `!` that need not be the complement is dropped and the branches swapped

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-COMMENT-BEFORE-KEPT
arms.note: a comment between the `!` and its operand is not seen, and the positive rebuild drops it

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-COMMENT-AFTER-KEPT
arms.note: a comment after the operand inside the dropped paren is not seen, and the positive rebuild drops it

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-COMMENT-WHOLE-COND
arms.note: a comment INSIDE the kept operand blocks the inversion too, though it travels verbatim

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-SWAP-OFF
arms.find: final kept: Null<QueryNode> = positive(cond, elseValue, site);
arms.note: a ternary built from a negated guard keeps the `!` (`x = !a ? 1 : 2`)

arms.name: M-INVERT-VALUE-CHAIN-SWAPPED
arms.find: if (sameConstruct(thenBranch, node, scan.seams) || sameConstruct(elseBranch, node, scan.seams)) return Skip;
arms.note: a ternary chain or else-if value chain is swapped, re-nesting it

arms.name: M-INVERT-VALUE-GLUE-BEFORE-BLIND
arms.note: a comment between the condition and the then-branch stays while the branches move

arms.name: M-INVERT-VALUE-GLUE-AFTER-BLIND
arms.note: a comment between the two branches stays while the branches move

arms.name: M-INVERT-VALUE-NO-DESCEND
arms.find: out.push(finding(scan, span, valueMessage(node, swap, seams) + COMMENT_BLOCKS));
arms.replace:
out.push(finding(scan, span, valueMessage(node, swap, seams) + COMMENT_BLOCKS));
						return;
arms.note: a report-only value form stops the walk, so an invertible conditional inside it is never fixed

arms.name: M-INVERT-VALUE-DESCEND-FIXED
arms.find:
out.push(finding(scan, span, valueMessage(node, swap, seams)));
						return;
arms.note: a fixable value form does not stop the walk, so a nested one is rewritten in the same pass (overlapping edits)

arms.name: M-INVERT-VALUE-UNGUARDED
arms.replace: edits.concat([for (g in guarded) { span: g.span, text: g.text }])
arms.note: value splices skip the parse round-trip: `!(a = b) ? 1 : 2` becomes `a = b ? 2 : 1`

arms.name: M-INVERT-VALUE-LOOSE-SPAN
arms.note: a splice over a node span that runs on through trailing trivia welds the condition to the `?` (`a? 2 : 1`)

arms.name: M-PTR-NO-ORIENT
arms.note: prefer-ternary-return writes `return !c ? a : b;` again

arms.name: M-PTR-TRAILING-SWAPS
arms.note: a guard's own trailing comment is left riding the value that moved to the `:` slot

arms.name: M-RRT-NO-ORIENT
arms.note: return-reassign-ternary writes `return !c ? e : x;` again

arms.name: M-PTA-NO-ORIENT
arms.note: prefer-ternary-assignment writes `x = !c ? a : b;` again, in both arms

arms.name: M-PTE-NO-ORIENT
arms.note: prefer-ternary-expression writes `!c ? a : b` again

arms.name: M-RETURN-CHAIN-COMMENT-ADMITTED
arms.note: the flat guard-chain rewrite drops a comment inside the chain

arms.name: M-PIEC-FIX-REPORT-INDEX
arms.find: OperatorSelection.of(plugin, [{ file: file, source: source }], index)
arms.note: the chain rule's fix reads a chain over a sibling module's overloading type as one the switch rule claims, and drops the edit its run reported

arms.name: M-PIEC-RUN-SELECTION
arms.find: for (m in collect(plugin, entry.file, entry.source, seams, resolveIndex, selection))
arms.replace: for (m in collect(plugin, entry.file, entry.source, seams, resolveIndex, OperatorSelection.of(plugin, [entry])))
arms.note: the chain rule asks a per-file operator table, which sees no overload a sibling module declares, and leaves a chain the switch rule refuses to nobody

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-KEEP-DEFAULT-BLIND
arms.note: `keepDefaultElse` never keeps a negation: `!a ? x : null` is still inverted to `a ? null : x` with the option on

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-KEEP-DEFAULT-ON
arms.note: `keepDefaultElse` is read as on when no config sets it, so every project silently stops inverting `!a ? x : null`

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-KEEP-DEFAULT-NO-RETURN
arms.note: a statement else branch `return null;` is not read through to its value, so `if (!a) return x; else return null;` is inverted

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-KEEP-DEFAULT-NO-BLOCK
arms.note: a braced else branch `{ return false; }` is not read through, so it is inverted while the bare one is kept

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-KEEP-DEFAULT-NO-PAREN
arms.note: a parenthesised default `!a ? x : (null)` is no default arm and is inverted

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-KEEP-DEFAULT-ANY-LITERAL
arms.note: every else arm counts as a default, so `!a ? x : 1` is no longer inverted under the option

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-KEEP-DEFAULT-THEN-ARM
arms.note: a ternary builder asks the gate about the THEN value: `if (!a) y = x; else y = 0;` is oriented positive to `y = a ? 0 : x;` under the option

arms.name: M-PTR-KEEP-DEFAULT-THEN-ARM
arms.note: prefer-ternary-return asks the gate about the guard value: `if (!a) return x; return null;` becomes `return a ? null : x;` under the option

arms.name: M-INVERT-KEEP-DEFAULT-STATEMENT-THEN-ARM
arms.note: an if statement is gated on its THEN branch: `if (!a) return null; else return x;` is no longer inverted under the option

arms.name: M-INVERT-KEEP-DEFAULT-VALUE-THEN-ARM
arms.note: a value form is gated on its THEN arm: `!a ? null : x` is no longer reported under the option

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-SWAP-DEFAULT-LAST-DROPPED
arms.find: final turned: Null<String> = defaultLastCondition(cond, thenArm, elseArm, site);
arms.note: the swap never asks the `defaultLast` turn: `a ? null : x` stays default-first under the option

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-SWAP-DEFAULT-LAST-ARMS-SWAPPED
arms.note: the turn reads the arms the wrong way round: `a ? null : x` is left and `a ? x : null` is turned default-first

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-DEFAULT-LAST-ANY-COND
arms.note: any condition is turned: a compound or an ordered comparison is wrapped `!( … )` instead of being left

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-DEFAULT-LAST-BOTH-LITERALS
arms.note: two literals are turned too: `a ? 0.0 : 1.0` becomes `!a ? 1.0 : 0.0`

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-DEFAULT-LAST-THEN-ANY
arms.note: a non-default then arm is turned: `a ? x : y` becomes `!a ? y : x`

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-DEFAULT-LAST-RETURN-MISMATCH
arms.note: a returning then arm is turned against a non-returning else statement: `if (a) return null; else g();`

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-DEFAULT-LAST-OVERLOAD-BLIND
arms.note: the `!` added and the `==` flipped are never asked of the operator table: an `@:op(!A)` / `@:op(A == B)` abstract is turned

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-DEFAULT-LAST-EQ-UNASKED
arms.note: only the not is asked: an `@:op(A == B)` without its `!=` twin is flipped

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-DEFAULT-LAST-BOOL-COND
arms.note: a bool-literal condition is turned: `true ? null : x` becomes `!true ? x : null`

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-DEFAULT-LAST-ON
arms.note: `defaultLast` is read as on when no config sets it, so every project silently turns `a ? null : x`

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-DEFAULT-LAST-NO-KEEP
arms.note: `defaultLast` no longer implies `keepDefaultElse`: `!a ? x : null` is inverted back to `a ? null : x` and the two directions ping-pong

arms.name: M-INVERT-DEFAULT-LAST-VALUE-MESSAGE
arms.note: a default-last turn of a ternary is worded as a dropped negation

arms.name: M-INVERT-DEFAULT-LAST-STATEMENT-MESSAGE
arms.note: a default-last turn of an if statement is worded as a dropped negation

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-DEFAULT-LAST-INTERPOLATION-AS-LITERAL
arms.note: an interpolating string reads as a literal, so `folder ? null : '${item.id}'` is left default-first

arms.name: M-PIER-MERGE-ANY-VALUE
arms.note: any repeated value merges, so two equal calls (or field reads typed under different narrowings) become one ternary branch

arms.name: M-PIER-MERGE-UNMARCHABLE
arms.note: a statement-like value merges into a ternary branch the pairwise march would refuse

arms.name: M-PIER-MERGE-COMMENT
arms.find: if (comments.exists(tok -> tok.to > region.from && tok.from < region.to)) return null;
arms.note: a merge ignores comments in its region, and the rebuild drops them

arms.name: M-PIER-MERGE-ANY-COUNT
arms.find: if (from < 0 || from > 0 && from >= rungs.length) return null;
arms.note: only a run of exactly three merges, so the mergeable tail of a longer run keeps its statements

arms.name: M-PIER-LEADING-AS-OUTER
arms.find: if (valueText(values[1], source, comments) == repeated) return Leading;
arms.note: two leading branches with one value no longer merge by `||`

arms.name: M-PIER-REWRITES-FOLDED
arms.note: every owned chain is rewritten, so a two-branch chain with a ternary tail becomes a three-branch value chain the author never wrote

arms.name: M-PIER-CLAIMSCHAIN-OWNS
arms.note: the chain claim answers ownership, so `redundant-else-after-return` loses its de-nest on a chain this rule leaves alone

arms.name: M-PIER-CASCADE-UNMERGED-REPORTED
arms.replace: final merge: Null<Merge> = m == null ? null : m.merge ?? { shape: Leading, from: 0, span: m.prefix, prefix: m.prefix };
arms.note: an owned cascade that does not merge is reported, with no fix behind the finding

arms.name: M-PIER-OUTER-UNNEGATED
arms.find: case Outer: NegationScan.negateConditionText(m.conds[rung], source, s.negation, emit.logic, emit.types());
arms.note: the outer merge keeps the first condition positive, inverting which branch returns what

arms.name: M-PIER-MERGE-NO-PARENS
arms.note: no merged piece is a ParenGuard hole, so a ternary condition re-associates across the new `&&`

arms.name: M-PIER-TAIL-REPORTED-AT-HEAD
arms.note: a merged tail is reported and keyed at the run head, so the finding names a guard the edit does not touch

arms.name: M-PIER-TAIL-SPAN-WHOLE
arms.find: final span: Span = new Span(start.from, region.to);
arms.note: a merged tail replaces the whole run, dropping the guards in front of it

arms.name: M-PIER-TAIL-FROM-FOLDED
arms.find: if (from < 0 || from > 0 && from >= rungs.length) return null;
arms.replace: if (from < 0 || from > 0 && from > rungs.length) return null;
arms.note: a tail may start at a value folded out of the terminal ternary, past the last written rung

arms.name: M-PIER-TAIL-LADDER
arms.find: return shape == null || from > 0 && repeatsTail(values[from - 1], tail, source, comments) ? null : {
arms.note: a tail merges although the value before it repeats one of its own, so a guard ladder merges again on every pass into one nested condition

arms.name: M-ASYM-FIX-NO-EDIT
arms.note: no bare branch is ever braced, so asymmetric-branch-braces stays report-only although the wrap is the writer's symmetric repair

arms.name: M-ASYM-FIX-UNTERMINATED
arms.note: a bare branch with no terminator of its own is braced: `if (a) p() else { … }` becomes `{ p() }`, which Haxe rejects with Missing ;

arms.name: M-ASYM-FIX-NESTED-OVERLAP
arms.find: if (edits.exists(e -> taken.exists(t -> e.span.from < t.span.to && t.span.from < e.span.to)))
arms.note: a pair inside a bare branch the same call braces gets its own edit, nested inside the outer one

arms.name: M-ASYM-FIX-DECL
arms.note: a bare declaration branch is braced, scoping its binding

arms.name: M-ASYM-FIX-NO-TERMINATOR-ADDED
arms.note: an unterminated bare expression statement is braced without its terminator: `{ p() }`, which Haxe rejects with Missing ;

arms.name: M-ASYM-FIX-CHAIN-TAIL-ONLY
arms.note: only the flagged tail pair of an else-if chain is braced, leaving `if (a) x(); else if (b) { y(); } else { … }` braced in its tail and bare in its head

arms.name: M-ASYM-FIX-OPEN-TAIL-ANY
arms.note: any unterminated bare branch takes an appended terminator, a conditional-compilation region included, whose terminator its parent owns

arms.name: M-REDUNDANT-BRACES-DANGLING-ELSE
arms.note: a block holding an else-less conditional loses its braces where an else follows, and that else re-binds onto the inner if

arms.name: M-REDUNDANT-BRACES-DECL
arms.note: a block holding one declaration loses its braces, widening the binding's scope

arms.name: M-REDUNDANT-BRACES-ASYMMETRIC
arms.note: a chain whose else must stay braced is stripped in its then branch alone, leaving the asymmetry asymmetric-branch-braces reports

arms.name: M-REDUNDANT-BRACES-COMMENT
arms.note: a block with a comment between a brace and its statement is reported, though stripping its braces would drop or misplace the comment

arms.name: M-ASYM-CHAIN-UNFLAGGED
arms.note: a chain whose braced and bare branches disagree outside its tail pair - one with no final else - is not a finding, although the writer symmetric mode braces it

arms.name: M-ASYM-CHAIN-PER-LINK
arms.note: every else-if link is read as the head of a chain of its own, so one chain reports its tail pair once per link above it

arms.name: M-ASYM-CHAIN-PAIR-SKIPPED
arms.note: an asymmetric tail pair is reported as the whole chain, losing the message that names which branch is braced

arms.name: M-ASYM-CHAIN-SWITCH-BRACED
arms.note: a terminal else switch counts as a bare branch, so a braced chain ending in one is flagged and its switch braced, though the writer glues it to its else

arms.name: M-ASYM-FIX-COMMENT-OUTSIDE
arms.note: a bare branch is braced around its statement alone, leaving its own comments between the header and the `{`

arms.name: M-ASYM-TRY-UNFLAGGED
arms.note: a try/catch whose body is braced and whose catch is bare is not a finding, although the writer symmetric mode braces the catch

arms.name: M-ASYM-TRY-FIX-NO-EDIT
arms.note: no bare body of an asymmetric try/catch is ever braced, so the try half of asymmetric-branch-braces stays report-only

arms.name: M-ASYM-TRY-FIX-UNTERMINATED
arms.note: a bare expression body is braced without a terminator, `{ p() }`, which Haxe rejects as Missing ;

arms.name: M-COLLAPSE-CALL-OUTER-EXTRACTOR
arms.note: an extractor in an outer pattern shares or reorders the evaluation of the moved call

arms.name: M-COLLAPSE-CALL-READS-BOUND
arms.note: a call reading a name the outer or an inner pattern binds is evaluated outside that binding after the splice

arms.name: M-COLLAPSE-CALL-WILDCARD-ARM
arms.note: a guarded or non-trailing wildcard inner arm becomes a dropped wildcard extractor, so the call is skipped or reordered

arms.name: M-COLLAPSE-CALL-READS-INTERPOLATED
arms.note: a call reading a bound name only through string interpolation is moved past that binding

arms.name: M-COLLAPSE-TYPED-COVERAGE
arms.note: an inner switch with no catch-all stays refused though its arms match every constructor of the subject enum

arms.name: M-COLLAPSE-CALL-OR-WILDCARD
arms.note: an or-pattern of wildcards loses the call the matcher drops
